name: Example: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector With Respect to a Given Basis in a Polynomial Vector Space
problem:
Consider the following polynomials:

$$
p_1(t)=5+t^2, \quad
p_2(t)=3t-2t^2, \quad
q(t)=5-3t+3t^2.
$$

If $\mathcal{B}=\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\},$ find $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}.$
worked_solution:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that 

$$
x_1 p_1(t)+x_2 p_2(t) = q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(5+{t}^{2})+{x}_{2}(3t-2{t}^{2}) & =5-3t+3{t}^{2} \\ 5{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}t+({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}){t}^{2} & =5-3t+3{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}=5 \\ 3{x}_{2}=-3 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068026/assets/195a50f130cc40c4a725066035f2da3ef25b725df96601e53f70716bd82b4f4a.png)

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{5}){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}=5 \\ 3{x}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the first and second equations, we get $x_1=1$ and $x_2 =-1.$ Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068026/assets/9f23f71e833d7a7f81f511e1dfb72861ed753cb514de43d6cabfeb3c6b65fadb.png)
